text:
Maya (support): FYI ParcelFlow is seeing a big spike this morning, ~10:15 UTC, lots of 429s reported by their frontend. Customer says it's degrading checkout flows.
Alex (ParcelFlow): Yep — we started getting 429 responses around 10:12. Frontend shows rapid retries, users see failures. Not sure why? We haven't changed code.
Maya (support): Can you paste a sample response headers & status from the failing requests? Any X-RateLimit headers?
Alex (ParcelFlow): Sample: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:13:02 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining-RPM: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 00:00:30
Content-Type: application/json
```
Maya (support): Thanks — that looks like an RPM limit hit (Remaining 0). Are you on the Standard plan with per-minute caps?
Sam (solutions): ParcelFlow, can you confirm request pattern: are these many parallel single-token streaming calls or short non-streamed requests? Also SDK version?
Alex (ParcelFlow): Non-streaming POSTs to /v1/generate, around 30 requests/sec sustained for a few minutes. SDK v1.2.3. No streaming.
Raj (oncall): Quick check: are they using connection pooling / keepalive? Lots of short-lived TCP connections can spike token accounting.
Alex (ParcelFlow): We use default HTTP client in Node, not explicitly reusing keepalive.
Tina (eng-infra): Two immediate mitigations: 1) advise the customer to enable HTTP keep-alive and connection reuse. 2) add jittered exponential backoff on 429s. We can also offer a temporary minute-cap bump while we triage.
Maya (support): ParcelFlow — we can apply a 5-minute bump to your RPM by +30% to ease user impact while you implement client changes. Want us to do that?
Alex (ParcelFlow): Yes please, that would help for now. Also can you recommend concrete retry settings?
Sam (solutions): Recommended client-side pattern: on 429, backoff = base * 2^attempt + random(0, base). Base ~200ms, max backoff 10s, max attempts 6. Also cap concurrency to ~5 per user/session to avoid thundering.
Raj (oncall): I'll also check internal throttling logs — looking for minute boundary alignment issues (requests all hitting the rollover at the same second).
SRE-Bot: ingest_log: matched 429 spike pattern for tenant parcelflow (tenant_id: tf_834). Peak RPM 1620 at 10:13:01 UTC, sustained ~90s. Suspected pattern: high parallel short requests.
Tina (eng-infra): ParcelFlow, please run this quick local repro to confirm you see the same pattern (node curl loop):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' & done; wait
```
If you see rapid 429s, try again with an HTTP client that reuses sockets.
Alex (ParcelFlow): Running now, will report.
Maya (support): While they run, Raj — can you check token refill stamps and per-tenant rate windows? Also confirm whether we applied any global emergency throttle at that time.
Raj (oncall): Looking... no global emergency throttle. Per-tenant policy shows soft base 1200 RPM, enforcement kicked in at 10:12:58 when remaining hit 0. Refill rate seems normal.
Tina (eng-infra): If they can't upgrade plan immediately, longer-term we should add advisory in docs about: keepalive, multiplexing, batching small prompts into fewer calls, and client concurrency limits. Also consider offering SDK helpers for built-in backoff.
Alex (ParcelFlow): Repro script produced identical 429s when we fire 200 parallel short requests; switching to persistent agent (keepalive) reduced peak RPM and avoided 429s in our local test. Good catch.
Sam (solutions): Great — so short-term: we apply the +30% RPM for 5 minutes, advise keepalive and retry changes. Mid-term: plan upgrade or quota increase, and SDK changes.
Maya (support): ParcelFlow — I've opened a temporary quota bump (ticket #SUP-1822) for 5 minutes starting 10:18 UTC. You should see fewer errors now. Please roll out client change and let us know when complete. :thumbsup:
Alex (ParcelFlow): Thanks everyone. Applying keepalive now to prod, will monitor.
Raj (oncall): Follow-ups for infra: consider adding a per-tenant burst buffer metric to surface imminent RPM exhaustion earlier in Console. Filing infra follow-up ticket.
Tina (eng-infra): Filing ENG-PRQ-558: console alert for 'tenant RPM approaching limit' with 5-min lookahead.
Maya (support): Closing this thread once ParcelFlow confirms reduced errors. If 429s persist after the client change and bump, we'll escalate to runtime team for deeper kernel-level investigation.
Alex (ParcelFlow): Errors dropped to near zero after keepalive and bump. Thanks all. :rocket:
